title: C914 — Rain sensor connector
introduction:
The rain sensor's connector brings electrical supply, communication and ground into the same housing. I read those roles separately: the communication connection carries messages, rather like a conversation sharing the room with the power socket. LIN means local interconnect network, a data link between a controller and nearby electronic devices.

Start with the identity table, match the drawing's cavity labels to the pin rows, then consult the service-parts table for catalogue references. This is a connector-reading guide. Physical viewing direction, access, test conditions, wire selection and replacement need separate instructions; gauge conventions and Size and Used codes are not decoded here.

edits.why: The drawing shows a vertical cavity stack beside a tall projecting rib, with a smaller projection on the left side of the outline. I use those visible features to keep the page view oriented, then follow the printed cavity labels into the table. The shell-and-harness row identifies the record associated with this illustration.

Match each illustrated cavity label to its row and read through to Terminal Part Number. The function descriptions distinguish supply, LIN messages and ground return. The supply wording retains a fuse-or-circuit-breaker alternative without choosing between them. Read the terminal column individually: the communication row has a different terminal listing from the other circuit roles. These descriptions identify connections, not expected test results.

The kit row links Number with Service Part and Engineering Shell, alongside its own gauge, material and cavity information. I keep that service-assembly record separate from the circuit-wire gauges and individual terminal references above.
